To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the N-terminal domain (NTD) of E. coli DnaB helicase forms an octameric complex with a novel quaternary structure.
the N-terminal domain is an independent entity of the Dna helicase, that it binds ATP, and that it is structurally similar to the helix-hairpin-helix (HHH) domain of the RecA protein.

the N-termini of DnaB helicase are important for the assembly of the hexamer and for the interaction between the helicase and the DNA polymerase, and that the N-terminal domains of DnaB and the DNA polymerizing domain of DnaG interact with each other.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and mechanism of the hexameric helix-helix junction.
the structure, dynamics and mechanism of the DNA helicases, which play a key role in DNA replication and repair.
understanding the mechanism of DNA replication in bacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the crystal structure of DnaB NTD is the first to be determined for a bacterial replicative helicase.
the structure of the NTD is not a helicase domain.
the structure of the DNA helicase DnaB is a helix bundle, which is a novel fold for a helicase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to solve the structure of the NTD of DnaB helicase, which is the first structure of the N terminal domain of a hexameric helixase.
we have solved the first structure of the N-terminus of a DnaB hexamer, a key component of the replisome.
we were able to determine the structure of the N-terminus of a helicase and that we have shown that the structure is a dimer of dimers and that this is likely the structure in solution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DnaB N-terminal domain is a novel DNA binding domain.
the NTD of DnaB is a novel helicase domain that is essential for DNA unwinding and for DnaB's interaction with the replication fork.
the NTD of DnaB is a highly dynamic domain, which can adopt multiple conformations, depending on its environment.
